newsitem.title: INDIA: Hindu party faces setback in two Indian states.
newsitem.headline: Hindu party faces setback in two Indian states.

text.p: India's main opposition Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) faced a setback on Monday after the governor of the western state of Gujarat asked it to prove its majority in the local assembly following a split in party ranks.

The BJP was also worried over developments in Uttar Pradesh where rival groups were preparing to install a non-BJP government after inconclusive polls in the state of 140 million people earlier this month, newspapers said.
The move comes despite the Hindu-nationalist party winning the most seats, but not a majority, in the 425-member Uttar Pradesh state assembly.
The BJP won 177 seats, while the rival United Front coalition of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda won 134 seats.
In Gujarat, the Press Trust of India said the BJP and the splinter Mahagujarat Janata Party (MJP) had been asked to prove their claims of majority in the state on Tuesday.
Gujarat was brought under New Delhi's direct rule last month after the BJP split into two there, forcing the fall of its government in one of India's most prosperous regions.

The Indian Express said on Monday the MJP had mustered a majority in the 181-member assembly with the help of the Congress party of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, which has 44 deputies there.

The same day, politicians said a move had gained support for a rapprochement between the Congress and Deve Gowda in Uttar Pradesh, effectively sidelining the BJP's claim to form a government in India's most populous state.

For the BJP, Uttar Pradesh is seen as crucial to the party's hopes of recapturing power in the federal government after briefly forming a minority administration earlier this year after general elections. The party remains the single largest group in the diverse federal parliament.
Its arch rival, the Congress Party, contested the Uttar Pradesh polls in an alliance with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), representing the lowest Hindu castes.
Although the BSP-Congress alliance won just 100 seats, Congress wanted the United Front, with 134 seats, to support former BSP chief minister Mayawati as chief minister.
The claim was opposed by Defence Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav, whose Samajawadi Party is the main arm of the United Front in the state.
But Yadav resigned his assembly seat on Sunday, paving the way for negotiations for a United-Front-Congress-BSP candidate in Uttar Pradesh, politicians said.
"We hope to form a stable government in a week," Uttar Pradesh Congress spokesman Ramesh Dixit said in the state capital of Lucknow.
